FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration.targets: Retired from the atlas on 2026-09-16, so there is no extract; read from data/atlas.json and its README. LI.0 audits the pinned libraries; LI.1–LI.3 inventory commutative algebra, analysis and category theory and supply missing universal properties; LI.4 publishes a declaration-level import ledger for NumberFieldArithmetic, LocalFieldsRamification, ClassFieldTheory, Chebotarev, ModularForms, EllipticCurves and others, scheduling their missing proofs; LI.5 adds axiom gates. No mathematical endpoint theorem.

Targets: finite extensions of a nonarchimedean local field are local fields; intrinsic e and f; the structure of K^× (deep-unit log/exp, power-class counts, open power subgroups); unramified extensions with Frobenius and Gal(K^ur/K) ≅ Ẑ; Eisenstein, tame and wild extensions; lower and upper numbering with Herbrand functions; Hasse–Arf; the different; and the tame quotient of G_K with its Iwasawa presentation.

judgements.reason: Foundations (now retired) only inventories Mathlib's existing algebra, analysis and category theory, leaving small gaps such as Fitting ideals, dualizing modules and the Grothendieck spectral sequence; its LI.4 ledgers the supplier roadmaps and schedules their missing proofs rather than proving them. LocalFieldsRamification must still build finite extensions of local fields, unramified theory with Frobenius and K^ur ≅ Ẑ, upper numbering with Herbrand functions and Hasse–Arf, and the tame Iwasawa presentation.

EllipticCurves still needs the degree form, dual and Vélu isogenies, the Weil pairing and Tate modules, the Hasse bound, Tate's algorithm, the Tate curve, Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich (which itself uses local inertia), global minimal models and cohomological Selmer groups. LocalFieldsRamification's remaining unit-group structure, unramified theory, ramification filtrations with Hasse–Arf and tame presentation are fewer layers, and Tau Ceti already has part of its layers 0–1.

ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations consumes the elliptic-curve torsion and Weil pairing that EllipticCurves still lacks, and adds Weil–Deligne representations, Artin/Swan conductors, Dickson's classification, Chebotarev recognition, abelian schemes (Picard algebraic spaces, Raynaud's theorems, Cartier duality) over the Hilbert-scheme and Artin-representability core, local class field theory and Chebotarev density. EllipticCurves stays at the level of Weierstrass equations and local fields.

ReductiveGroups already has layers 0–2 and 4, and what remains (Borel and torus conjugacy, general root data, Bruhat, the isomorphism and existence theorems, Chevalley–Demazure over ℤ) is one deep but self-contained stack. ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations is unbuilt, and it stacks abelian schemes (Picard spaces via Artin representability, Raynaud's theorems) on the Hilbert-scheme and stack core, together with local class field theory, Chebotarev density, ramification theory and Dickson's classification.

AlgebraicModuli must build Hilbert and Quot schemes, algebraic spaces and stacks, coarse spaces, Artin representability and characteristic-zero resolution of singularities, and it imports AdicSpacesPartII's rigid-analytic and formal foundations (F0, R0–R3); the baseline has none of this. ReductiveGroups already has layers 0–2 and 4 complete and most others partial, and its remaining conjugacy, classification and Chevalley–Demazure work is narrower.

ExponentialSums' base layer ES.0 imports the Weil and Deligne bounds (FF.2), so it rests on Weil I/II with étale cohomology, duality and Lefschetz pencils (whose recorded closure even reaches AlgebraicModuli's R09.1–R09.4 core), plus zero-density estimates, the large sieve and Vinogradov mean values. AlgebraicModuli's own stacks, Artin representability, resolution of singularities and rigid-analytic imports are also enormous, and without the imported Weil–Deligne bounds it would be the farther one.

ExponentialSums imports the Weil and Deligne bounds at ES.0 and so rests on Weil I/II with étale cohomology and Lefschetz pencils, beneath its own Vinogradov mean-value, circle-method, zero-density and large-sieve work. BelyiMaps' long chain (covers, analytic Riemann existence, analytic Riemann–Roch, algebraization, Belyi's theorem, profinite π₁ and branch-cycle) is classical one-variable theory, and Tau Ceti already has part of its base (permutation triples, universal-cover classification, function-field Riemann–Roch).

BelyiMaps must prove a deep chain of theorems: π₁ of the thrice-punctured sphere, filled branched covers, analytic Riemann existence, algebraization via analytic Riemann–Roch, Belyi's theorem with descent, the profinite π₁ comparison, branch-cycle and faithfulness. GeometricTopology is broader (gluing, tubular neighbourhoods, the Reidemeister and Markov theorems, Mostow volume invariance, Heegaard existence, Whitehead's PL reconciliation), but it only states its Kirby targets and several of its layers are already partly built.

AdicSpacesPartII needs rigid-analytic foundations (fibre products, analytification and GAGA, Raynaud generic fibres, Kiehl coherence, formal GAGA, dagger spaces) on top of the unfinished Tau Ceti AdicSpaces layers, and for sousperfectoid families it imports almost purity, Huber's étale geometry and the ∞-categorical sheaves E0–E1. GeometricTopology's differential, PL and knot-theoretic infrastructure, with a few deep proofs such as Mostow invariance and Reidemeister, sits much closer to Mathlib's manifold library.

AdicSpacesPartII already needs EnhancedDerivedSheaves' core E0–E1 (through classical étale sheaves in its sousperfectoid layer), and it adds rigid-analytic and formal geometry, perfectoid almost purity and Huber's étale geometry on top of the unfinished Tau Ceti AdicSpaces layers. EnhancedDerivedSheaves' extra E2–E5 (Postnikov and hypercover descent, the adjoint functor theorem, symmetric monoidal ∞-categories, animated rings, the spectra comparison) is also very large, so the margin is small.

Lefschetz's dependencies (through E2, the étale six-functor theory EDC.0–EDC.6 and diamond étale cohomology) already contain E0–E4 and E5's abstract and animated parts, and its later layers also need Weil II and abelian schemes. EnhancedDerivedSheaves adds only Ind-completion and the spectra and K-theory comparison beyond that.

SmoothRepresentations' SR.6 imports the Fargues–Scholze machinery (excursion operators, parameter stacks, Bun_G strata, geometric Satake, sheaves on v-stacks), whose dependencies include almost all of Lefschetz's (étale six functors, Weil II, diamonds), and SR.4 and SR.2a–SR.3 add Bruhat–Tits decompositions, dual groups and Bernstein's theory. Lefschetz's own nearby-cycle, Picard–Lefschetz and monodromy layers are the smaller part.

ModularIwasawa's suppliers (Skinner–Urban congruences on unitary Shimura varieties, Kato and Heegner Euler systems, Hida families, p-adic Hodge regulators, BSD branches) bring modular curves, Shimura varieties, modularity lifting, p-adic Hodge theory and Iwasawa cohomology, and their closure includes SmoothRepresentations itself. SmoothRepresentations adds beyond that only the Fargues–Scholze parameter machinery and its own Bernstein and Satake theory.

Foundations is a retired inventory-and-process roadmap whose own gaps are small (Fitting ideals, dualizing modules, the Grothendieck spectral sequence). GeometricTopology must build gluing and tubular neighbourhoods, knot presentations with the Reidemeister and Markov theorems, Dehn surgery, concordance, hyperbolic volume with Mostow invariance, JSJ and Heegaard objects, Euler classes of foliations and the PL reconciliation.

ModularIwasawa's dependencies include nearly all of EnhancedDerivedSheaves' stages (through p-adic Hodge theory, derived de Rham and étale cohomology) plus hundreds of stages of arithmetic geometry: Shimura varieties, Euler systems, p-adic Hodge theory, Iwasawa cohomology and automorphic congruences. EnhancedDerivedSheaves is a foundational ∞-categorical layer with no arithmetic endpoint.

SmoothRepresentations' dependencies already contain AlgebraicModuli's R09.1–R09.4 and Artin-representability core (through Weil restriction for dual groups and the abelian-scheme inputs of its étale suppliers), and add Bruhat–Tits theory and, for SR.6, the Fargues–Scholze apparatus with étale six functors, Weil II and diamonds. AlgebraicModuli's only unshared parts are coarse spaces, algebraization and characteristic-zero resolution.

ExponentialSums rests on the Weil and Deligne bounds it imports at ES.0 (Weil I/II with étale cohomology and Lefschetz pencils), beneath Vinogradov mean values, the circle method, zero-density estimates and the large sieve. ReductiveGroups already has layers 0–2 and 4 complete, and its remaining conjugacy, root-datum, classification and Chevalley–Demazure work is a narrower algebraic stack.

ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations needs abelian schemes via Picard algebraic spaces and Artin representability, Raynaud's finite-flat theorem, local class field theory for Weil groups, Chebotarev density and ramification filtrations, on top of its own Weil–Deligne, conductor and Dickson layers. BelyiMaps' heaviest imports are analytic Riemann–Roch and algebraic-curve models, over a combinatorial and covering-space base that Tau Ceti has partly built.

Lefschetz's dependencies (through EDC.6 and diamond étale cohomology) contain AdicSpacesPartII's formal layer F0 and all of its imports (perfectoid almost purity, adic étale geometry, E0–E1), and add étale six functors with perverse sheaves, Weil I/II and abelian schemes. AdicSpacesPartII adds only its own rigid-analytic layers R0–R5 and the dagger layer F1.

Foundations only inventories existing general theory and ledgers supplier roadmaps; its LI.4 takes EllipticCurves' pinned snapshot without proving what is missing. EllipticCurves itself must still build the dual isogeny, Weil pairing, Tate modules, Hasse bound, Tate's algorithm, Tate curve, Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich, global minimal models and Selmer groups.

LocalFieldsRamification is five layers of classical local-field theory, with the normalized valuation, unit filtration and Teichmüller lift already in Tau Ceti. GeometricTopology spans eleven layers of differential, PL and knot theory and of Riemannian and 3-manifold geometry, including tubular neighbourhoods, the Reidemeister and Markov theorems, Mostow volume invariance, Heegaard existence, Whitehead's reconciliation and an imported τ invariant.

ModularIwasawa's dependencies include all but one of AdicSpacesPartII's stages (its rigid-analytic foundations serve Shimura-variety and p-adic Hodge suppliers). On top of that it needs modularity, Euler systems, Iwasawa cohomology and automorphic congruences.

Both need the core of Hilbert schemes, algebraic spaces and stacks with Artin representability (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations through abelian schemes). AlgebraicModuli adds coarse spaces, algebraization, characteristic-zero resolution and rigid-analytic foundations, while ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations adds abelian schemes with Picard spaces and Raynaud's theorems, local class field theory, Chebotarev density, ramification theory, Dickson's classification and pseudo-representations, which I judge the larger remainder.

SmoothRepresentations presupposes the structure theory of reductive groups over local fields: it imports ReductiveGroupsPartII (Bruhat–Tits decompositions, dual groups), which rests on ReductiveGroups. On top of that it adds Bernstein's second adjointness and centre, the Satake isomorphism, Helm families and, for SR.6, the Fargues–Scholze machinery, while ReductiveGroups itself already has layers 0–2 and 4 complete.
